## Profile

Applied Mathematics PhD student at the University of Colorado Denver with experience in machine learning, statistical modeling, clinical natural language processing, high-performance computing, and mathematical research. Develops reproducible end-to-end data science systems spanning SQL data extraction, feature engineering, predictive modeling, model evaluation, operational ranking, and deployment-oriented monitoring.

Research interests include machine learning, neural networks, nonlinear and complex systems, representation learning, and the mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence. Experienced communicating technical results to researchers, operational stakeholders, students, and interdisciplinary teams.

## Experience

### Donor Alliance
**Data Science Intern**  
Denver, Colorado | Summer 2026

- Developed an end-to-end machine learning framework for predicting the probability of near-term onsite involvement from longitudinal organ-donation referral data, integrating structured clinical variables with free-text clinical documentation.
- Constructed a leakage-aware historical modeling dataset from SQL Server referral records using event-time feature engineering, clinical data cleaning, documentation auditing, and temporally defined prediction targets.
- Designed a referral-disjoint temporal evaluation framework using a 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% held-out test split to approximate prospective deployment on future referrals.
- Established operational baselines using global prevalence, hospital-level historical demand, and hierarchical hospital--shift--hour demand with validation-selected smoothing.
- Developed and compared structured logistic regression, frozen Bio_ClinicalBERT text models, combined structured-plus-text logistic regression, and fine-tuned multimodal ClinicalBERT architectures.
- Built a Combined Logistic Regression model integrating standardized structured features with PCA-reduced Bio_ClinicalBERT embeddings for lightweight deployment and active-referral scoring.
- Fine-tuned a multimodal ClinicalBERT model using separate structured and narrative encoders with attention-based modality fusion, staged transformer fine-tuning, early stopping, and validation-based model selection.
- Achieved held-out performance of **AUROC 0.827 and AUPRC 0.524** with the fine-tuned multimodal model, compared with **AUROC 0.784 and AUPRC 0.465** for the lightweight Combined Logistic Regression model.
- Developed retrospective active-referral ranking analyses using Precision@K, Recall@K, Lift@K, and NDCG@K to evaluate model performance under realistic staffing constraints.
- Built a deployment-oriented Python repository integrating SQL queries, shared preprocessing, ClinicalBERT embeddings, logistic-regression training, model artifact persistence, active referral scoring, and capacity-aware staff ranking.
- Developed technical documentation, model monitoring recommendations, and a prospective shadow-evaluation strategy for assessing discrimination, calibration, ranking performance, and model drift over time.
- Presented technical methods and operational findings using reproducible visualizations, mathematical explanations, and decision-focused reporting for interdisciplinary stakeholders.

## Selected Projects

### Near-Term Referral Prioritization with Multimodal Clinical Machine Learning

Developed during the Donor Alliance Data Science Internship.

- Designed an event-level prediction framework for estimating:
  
  \[
  P(\text{first relevant onsite involvement within 8 hours})
  \]

  using only information available at the historical prediction time.
- Integrated clinical laboratory values, physiologic measurements, referral characteristics, workflow variables, temporal features, and sanitized clinical narrative.
- Used Bio_ClinicalBERT to construct contextual clinical-text representations.
- Evaluated structured-only, text-only, combined logistic-regression, and fine-tuned multimodal architectures.
- Developed capacity-aware ranking methods that convert probabilities into operational priority lists for the top \(K\) active referrals.
- Designed retrospective decision-time replay and prospective monitoring strategies for evaluating real-world ranking performance.

### Combined Logistic Regression Deployment Pipeline

- Built a modular Python repository for training and deploying a multimodal logistic-regression referral-ranking model.
- Integrated SQL Server data extraction through SQLAlchemy and `pyodbc`.
- Automated historical feature configuration and documentation-rate auditing.
- Implemented structured preprocessing with imputation, missingness indicators, scaling, and categorical encoding.
- Generated frozen Bio_ClinicalBERT embeddings and reduced text representations using PCA.
- Tuned class-balanced logistic regression using validation AUPRC.
- Persisted complete preprocessing and model components as versionable `joblib` artifacts.
- Developed active-referral scoring and staff-capacity ranking workflows producing timestamped operational outputs.
- Documented future improvements including shared train/serve feature engineering, model versioning, embedding caching, feature-parity testing, and prospective drift monitoring.

### High-Dimensional Biological Representation Learning

- Developed GMVAE-based representation-learning models for high-dimensional biological datasets.
- Evaluated latent representations across multiple latent-space dimensions and mixture-component configurations.
- Used HPC infrastructure for scalable experimentation and reproducible model training.

### Complex Systems Simulation and Mathematical Modeling

- Designed computational experiments for nonlinear and complex-system models.
- Conducted parameter sweeps across high-dimensional parameter spaces.
- Analyzed emergent behavior and relationships between model parameters and system dynamics.
